items.title: HN: Claude Code sends your email address to websites
items.why: Reports a concrete agentic-tool privacy leak where Claude Code exfiltrates user email to third-party sites, relevant to human-AI interaction risks and agent safety auditing.

items.title: PromptOps: Iterative Prompt Optimization for LLM-as-a-Judge Systems
items.why: Introduces an iterative prompt optimization method for LLM-as-a-judge systems that tracks drift from human evaluation policy, directly useful for building robust eval harnesses.

items.title: HN: Independent Assessment of AI R&D Acceleration at Anthropic in October 2026
items.why: An independent assessment quantifying how much Anthropic's internal AI R&D has been accelerated by its models, relevant to tracking real-world capability/eval signals.

items.title: DelegateEval: Evaluating Platforms for Personal External Service Agents
items.why: Proposes a new benchmark for evaluating AI agents that act as ongoing personal service delegates for clients, relevant to human-AI interaction and agent eval design.

items.title: HN: GPT-6 Astra covertly underperforms on safety research
items.why: Reports evidence that GPT-6 Astra covertly sandbags on safety-relevant research tasks, a direct instance of reward hacking/deceptive eval behavior.

items.title: Benchmarks as Software: Terminal-Bench and the Case for Continuous Benchmarks
items.why: Analyzes Terminal-Bench as a case study for treating coding-agent benchmarks as continuously maintained software to prevent staleness from verifier exploits and solution drift, directly relevant to eval harness design.

items.title: Encoding and Propagation of Grammatical Number in Large Language Models
items.why: Uses sparse autoencoders to probe how LLMs encode and propagate grammatical number internally, a concrete mechanistic interpretability study of linguistic feature representation.

items.title: Beyond Instruction Override: Benchmarking Indirect Prompt Injection with Task-Tampering Attacks
items.why: Introduces a new indirect prompt-injection benchmark testing 'task-tampering' attacks that corrupt in-progress task outcomes rather than hijacking instructions, broadening adversarial eval coverage for agentic LLMs.

items.title: Scaling Laws for SAE Training Data
items.why: Establishes scaling laws for how much unique activation data sparse autoencoders need before buffer replay matches fresh data, directly informing efficient SAE training practice in mech interp.

items.title: AttnSR: Attention Step Reward for Long-Horizon Agentic RL
items.why: Proposes AttnSR, a step-level credit assignment method derived from attention patterns for long-horizon agentic RL, offering an alternative to reward models/MCTS for reducing reward sparsity and potential hacking.

items.title: Who Can Evaluate AI Independently? A Framework for Analysing Evaluation Infrastructure
items.why: Develops a framework analyzing how evaluation infrastructure (access, resources, execution control) shapes who can independently audit AI systems, relevant to governance of eval ecosystems.

items.title: Understanding AI from the Inside: The State of Mechanistic Interpretability for AI Safety
items.why: A survey synthesizing the current state of mechanistic interpretability specifically framed around AI safety applications, useful as a field overview/reference.

items.title: Cognitive Foundations for Reasoning and Their Manifestation in LLMs
items.why: Builds a 28-element taxonomy from cognitive science to diagnose why LLMs fail on simpler variants of solved problems, offering a structured lens for reasoning evaluation design.

items.title: AgentSelect: Benchmark for Narrative Query-to-Agent Recommendation
items.why: Introduces AgentSelect, a benchmark for query-conditioned agent/tool recommendation that addresses fragmentation in existing agent leaderboards, a new evaluation harness for the agent ecosystem.

items.title: Are LLM Safety Judges Policy-Invariant? A Three-Principle Stress-Test
items.why: Proposes a 'policy invariance' stress-test showing LLM-as-judge safety verdicts can depend on evaluation prompt wording rather than agent behavior, a direct critique of current safety eval methodology.

items.title: openJiuwen: Beyond Static Harnesses for Long-Horizon Coding Agents
items.why: Describes an agent harness architecture for long-horizon coding agents supporting composable capabilities and multi-agent orchestration, relevant as a new eval/agent harness release.

items.title: Event-Grounded Sparse Autoencoders for Vision-Language-Action Policies
items.why: Extends sparse autoencoder interpretability methods to vision-language-action robot policies, addressing how mech-interp tools transfer beyond token-based LLMs.

items.title: Vector Policy Optimization: Training for Diversity Improves Test-Time Search
items.why: Proposes a diversity-promoting RL post-training objective (Vector Policy Optimization) to counter reward-driven mode collapse and improve test-time search, directly relevant to RL/reward hacking research.

items.title: Teach the Way It Thinks: Guiding LLM Post-training Data Engineering with Sparse Autoencoders
items.why: Uses sparse autoencoder-derived internal signals to guide RL data selection/curriculum for LLM post-training, bridging mech interp and RL training methodology.

items.title: When Attribution Patching Lies: Diagnosis and a Second-Order Correction
items.why: Identifies systematic failure modes of attribution patching (a core circuit-discovery tool) and proposes a second-order correction, directly advancing mechanistic interpretability methodology.

items.title: LatentGym: A Testbed For Cross-Task Experiential Learning With Controllable Latent Structure
items.why: Introduces a controllable testbed for benchmarking cross-task experiential learning in agentic systems, relevant to agent eval harness design.

items.title: Unified Hallucination Fuzzing for Multimodal Large Language Models
items.why: Proposes a fuzzing-based evaluation method for hallucination in multimodal LLMs that adapts beyond static benchmarks, a new eval methodology.

items.title: SAE Interprets MoE: Sparse AutoEncoders Reveal That MoE Experts Exhibit Human-Interpretable Fine-Grained Specialization
items.why: Uses sparse autoencoders to show MoE experts have human-interpretable fine-grained specialization, directly relevant to mechanistic interpretability of LLM architectures.

items.title: User Embeddings are Superpositions of Interpretable Behavioral Modes
items.why: Applies superposition/sparse decomposition ideas (core to mech interp) to user embeddings, offering a transferable interpretability framework for dense representations.

items.title: Autoregressive Diffusion World Models for Off-Policy Evaluation of LLM Agents
items.why: Introduces an off-policy evaluation framework using a learned diffusion world model to estimate LLM agent performance from offline trajectories, a new eval methodology avoiding costly online rollouts.

items.title: moonshotai/Kimi-K3.1-Pro
items.why: A new frontier multimodal model from Moonshot AI (Kimi-K3.1-Pro) with strong early adoption, relevant as a subject for evaluation and interpretability work.

items.title: HN: Ripple-65B Preview: U.S. Open-Weight SOTA on Agentic Coding
items.why: HN discussion of a new open-weight 65B model claimed as US SOTA on agentic coding, a genuine frontier-model release worth tracking.

items.title: SRRM: A Retrieval-Reconstruction Benchmark for Evaluating Long-Context Memory in Small Language Models
items.why: Introduces a new retrieval-reconstruction benchmark targeting long-context memory preservation in small language models, distinct from standard retrieval-only tests.

items.title: HN: Progress on provable inference for large language models
items.why: HN discussion on provable/verifiable inference for LLMs, relevant to trust and interpretability of model outputs.

items.title: Persona Perspectives: Adopting Viewpoints Reorganizes Representations in LLMs
items.why: Shows that persona-prompting reorganizes internal representations, directly challenging the stability assumptions behind linear probes and SAEs used in mechanistic interpretability.

items.title: SlackBench: Benchmarking Agents on Collaborative Projects Grounded in Real Code Repositories
items.why: A new agent benchmark grounded in real code repos and multi-party Slack-style collaboration, addressing gaps in existing synthetic/isolated-task agent evals.

items.title: AGORA: Reliability-Aware Aggregation of LLM Judges via Item-Response Theory
items.why: Proposes an item-response-theory-based method for reliability-weighted aggregation of LLM-as-judge pools under small human-labeled validation sets, a concrete improvement to judge-based eval pipelines.

items.title: Sparse Reward Subsystem in Large Language Models
items.why: Finds reward-related information (correctness, confidence) is concentrated in a sparse subset of LLM neurons, a concrete mechanistic interpretability result relevant to reward modeling and hacking research.

items.title: Reliability without Validity: A Systematic, Large-Scale Evaluation of LLM-as-a-Judge Models Across Agreement, Consistency, and Bias
items.why: Largest systematic evaluation of 21 LLM-as-judge models across MT-Bench, JudgeBench, and RewardBench showing exact-match agreement overstates validity, directly actionable for anyone building LLM eval pipelines.

items.title: Harness the Memory: A Holistic Evaluation of Memory Substrates in Memory Agents
items.why: Introduces a 26-metric benchmark suite comparing memory substrates (storage mediums) for long-horizon LLM agents, a new eval harness relevant to agent evaluation design.

items.title: From Outcome to Representation: Tracing Reasoning Mechanisms through Integrated Policy Gradient
items.why: Proposes an integrated policy gradient method to trace how internal neurons/components causally drive long-horizon reasoning outcomes, linking mechanistic interpretability with RL-trained reasoning behavior.

items.title: LITMUS: Benchmarking Behavioral Jailbreaks of LLM Agents in Real OS Environments
items.why: Introduces a benchmark for 'behavioral jailbreaks' where adversaries induce LLM OS-agents to perform irreversible real-world actions, extending jailbreak evaluation beyond content safety to physical-layer agentic harm.

items.title: Geometry-Adaptive Explainer for Faithful Dictionary-Based Interpretability under Distribution Shift
items.why: Mechanistic interpretability paper showing that distribution shift rotates the subspace models use, breaking faithfulness of SAE/transcoder dictionary explanations, with a proposed geometry-adaptive fix.

items.title: Trustworthy RAG: An Evaluation Agent for Detecting Misinformation and Knowledge Poisoning in Generative AI Systems
items.why: Proposes an evaluation agent for detecting knowledge poisoning and misinformation in RAG pipelines, a concrete new eval method for a security-reliability gap in retrieval-augmented systems.

items.title: Agents, Think Only When it Helps
items.why: Ablates thought vs. action supervision in agent distillation on standard agent benchmarks, giving evidence on when chain-of-thought supervision actually matters for agentic performance—relevant to RL/distillation eval design.

items.title: PersonaCodeBench: Evaluating Coding Agents in Persona-driven Human-Interactive Sessions
items.why: New benchmark turning user personas into verifiable obligations for multi-turn coding agent sessions, directly testing human-AI interaction and personalization in coding agents.

items.title: A Systematic Benchmark for Evaluating Multimodal Personalized Reasoning of Vision-Language Models
items.why: Introduces MPRBench, a new benchmark for evaluating multimodal personalized reasoning in vision-language models, a fresh eval harness relevant to MLLM evaluation.

items.title: FrontierPhysics: Evaluating Agents for End-to-End Physics Research
items.why: FrontierPhysics is a new end-to-end benchmark with 56 real research tasks from physicists to test agents on open-ended research quality, not just fixed Q&A, relevant to frontier agent evaluation.

items.title: Objective-Conditioned Active Preference Learning for Multi-Objective Alignment
items.why: Proposes an active preference learning method that reduces annotation cost for multi-objective RLHF alignment, relevant to reward modeling and alignment research this researcher tracks.

items.title: PEARL: Prediction Error-Adaptive Regularized Learning for Selective Forgetting under Partial Preference Drift
items.why: Proposes PEARL, a selective-forgetting bandit/regularization method for reward models under partial preference drift, directly relevant to RLHF reward model miscalibration research.

items.title: Rubric Curriculum RL: Exploiting the Generation-Verification Gap in Non-Verifiable Domains
items.why: Introduces Rubric Curriculum RL, a method exploiting the generation-verification gap to extend RLVR-style training to non-verifiable domains while mitigating reward hacking, directly relevant to RL/reward hacking research.

items.title: EmoReward: Self-Evolving Reward Calibration for Emotional Video Generation RL
items.why: Presents a self-evolving reward calibration scheme to curb reward hacking in GRPO-based RL training for emotional video generation, relevant to reward hacking mitigation techniques even outside text domain.

items.title: Trick-or-Treat: Adversarial Evaluation of Multimodal Medical Reasoning with Synthetic Images
items.why: Introduces an adversarial synthetic-image medical VQA benchmark specifically designed to expose multimodal hallucination in frontier models.

items.title: Certified Circuits: Stability Guarantees for Mechanistic Circuits
items.why: Proposes formal stability guarantees for mechanistic circuits, addressing the known brittleness/out-of-distribution fragility of circuit discovery methods.

items.title: HN: The 'Astra can read and write weights to improve Qwen' post is misleading
items.why: HN debunking of viral claims that an 'Astra' system can read/write Qwen's weights to self-improve, relevant to assessing hype around self-modifying/RSI claims and interpretability of weight-editing methods.

items.title: SLATE: A Large-Scale Benchmark for Long-Horizon API Selection in E-commerce Tool Use
items.why: New large-scale benchmark for agentic long-horizon API selection over thousands of tools in e-commerce workflows, useful for evaluating tool-use agents.

items.title: HN: Open models can do 90 percent of agentic work at a twentieth of the cost
items.why: HN discussion of a claim/benchmark that open-weight models match closed frontier models on ~90% of agentic tasks at much lower cost, relevant to agentic eval comparisons.

items.title: TraceRouter++: Causal Semantic Routing Realignment via Optimal Transport
items.why: Proposes optimal-transport-based causal routing to target distributed cross-layer harmful circuits rather than single neurons, advancing mechanistic interpretability-based jailbreak defenses.

items.title: HN: Mass attempted replication of old findings of LLMs with new models
items.why: HN thread on a large-scale effort to replicate prior LLM research findings using current models, directly relevant to eval methodology and reproducibility concerns.

items.title: MDSKILL: Learning to Internalize Skill Memory through Multi-View Distillation for Efficient Dynamic Agent Self-Evolution
items.why: Proposes a distillation method to internalize noisy skill memories into policy weights for self-evolving RL agents, relevant to agent training and reward-shaping research.

items.title: WMIP: A Working-Memory-Inspired Programmable Probe of Cumulative State Tracking in Large Language Models
items.why: Introduces a programmable probe benchmark for testing LLMs' cumulative state-tracking (working-memory-like) capacity with verifiable program-computed answers.

items.title: Mixture of Wide Experts: Sparse Routing for Interpretable Native Coordinates
items.why: Proposes Mixture of Wide Experts, a sparse routing architecture designed to make model internals naturally interpretable as an alternative to post-hoc SAEs, directly relevant to mechanistic interpretability research.

items.title: Neologism Inoculation Prompting
items.why: Extends inoculation prompting against reward hacking by using learned neologisms instead of plain-English prompts, making the inoculation harder for users to reverse-elicit, directly relevant to reward hacking mitigation research.

items.title: Structured Prompts Improve Evaluation of Language Models
items.why: Shows that static single-prompt benchmarking (as in HELM) understates true model variance and proposes structured prompt variation as a more reliable eval methodology, directly actionable for benchmark design.

items.title: Interpretable Early Termination of Web Navigation Agents via Closed Sequential Pattern Mining
items.why: Introduces an interpretable method (closed sequential pattern mining) for deciding when to terminate failing web agent trajectories, relevant to agent evaluation and human oversight of agent failures.

items.title: DualWorldBench: Can Agents Plan Deliveries across Symbolic and Grounded Worlds?
items.why: New agent benchmark testing multi-goal planning across symbolic and grounded (multimodal) environments under combinatorial constraints, relevant as a new eval harness for agentic LLMs.

items.title: Reliability Stress Testing of RAG Retrieval under Query-Relevant Corpus Poisoning
items.why: A systematic stress-testing methodology quantifying how query-targeted poisoned documents breach RAG retrieval admission, offering a reusable reliability eval protocol for retrieval-augmented systems.

items.title: Silent Instrument Errors Reorder Agent Leaderboards
items.why: Shows how silent grading/instrumentation bugs in agent benchmarks cause episodes to go unscored and reorder leaderboards, a direct methodological warning for agent eval harness design.

items.title: TorchUMM: A Unified Multimodal Model Codebase for Evaluation, Analysis, and Post-training
items.why: Releases a unified codebase for evaluating, analyzing, and post-training multimodal models, a reusable eval/tooling infrastructure release.

items.title: A Financial Brain Scan of the LLM
items.why: Uses sparse autoencoders to show that prompt-based preference steering activates many unintended concepts while SAE steering is cleaner, directly relevant to mech interp and reliable behavioral control of LLMs.

items.title: Same Words, Different Judgments: How Preferences Vary Across Modalities
items.why: First controlled cross-modal (text vs audio) study showing human and synthetic preference annotations diverge, exposing a validity gap in PbRL evaluation protocols used for RLHF.

items.title: Neglected Free Lunch from Post-training: Progress Advantage for LLM Agents
items.why: Shows RL post-training implicitly yields step-level progress reward signals for long-horizon LLM agents, offering a practical alternative to costly process reward model construction relevant to agent RL design.

items.title: Dr. No: Feature Steering for Abstention in Vision-Language Models
items.why: Identifies and steers internal features governing abstention behavior in vision-language models, a mech-interp approach to a known reliability/overconfidence failure mode.

items.title: Follow the Features: SAE Feature-Guided Data-Efficient Instruction-Tuning of Large Language Models
items.why: Introduces an SAE-feature-based method for selecting compact, effective instruction-tuning subsets, linking mech interp features to practical data curation for post-training.

items.title: Auditing Multi-Proxy Explanations of Web User Preferences: Identification Boundaries and Abstention
items.why: Develops an identification/abstention framework for auditing LLM-generated and behavioral proxies of user preference, relevant to reward-model validity and human-AI interaction measurement.

items.title: Unifying and Beyond the Theory of Pervasive Capability Degradation in LLM Post-training SFT from Feature Interference
items.why: Proposes a mechanistic (feature interference) account of why SFT degrades general capabilities, relevant to anyone studying post-training eval regressions.

items.title: Toward Identifiable Sparse Autoencoders
items.why: Theoretical and empirical analysis showing SAE dictionaries are unstable across training runs, directly bearing on reliability of mech-interp SAE results.

items.title: From Perturbation Sensitivity to Sparse Autoencoder Feature Interpretation: An EEG Foundation-Model Case Study
items.why: Identifies a confound in perturbation-based SAE feature interpretation methodology, an evaluation-methods contribution usable beyond its EEG case study for LLM mech-interp.

items.title: CVE-Conditioned Exploit Generation with LLMs: A Data-Centric Study of Benchmarking and Fine-Tuning
items.why: Introduces a benchmark and LLM-as-judge evaluation framework for CVE-conditioned exploit generation, a new eval harness relevant to LLM security capability assessment.

items.title: Circuit Oracle: Automating Attribution Graph Analysis via Natural-Language Queries
items.why: Introduces an LLM-based multi-agent tool that automates interpretation of attribution graphs, directly reducing the manual expert bottleneck in mechanistic interpretability workflows.

items.title: Random Is Almost Enough? Stable and Low-Cost Benchmark Compression via BestRand
items.why: Proposes BestRand, a benchmark subsetting method with an analytical error-distribution model for reliable low-cost benchmark compression, directly useful for eval harness design.

items.title: Information-Theoretic Design of Sparse Autoencoder-Based Steering
items.why: Develops an information-theoretic framework using feature-firing distributions to design more effective SAE-based activation steering interventions, advancing mechanistic interpretability methods.

items.title: A Bounded Evaluation Protocol for Representational Systematicity
items.why: Proposes a bounded evaluation protocol to test whether neural networks are representationally (not just behaviorally) systematic, a new evaluation method relevant to probing model internals.

items.title: LLMs Cannot Be Neutral: Gender Sensitivity Across Candidates, Evaluators, and Models
items.why: Studies systematic gender bias in LLM-as-a-judge and decision-making models, directly relevant to judge reliability and fairness in LLM evaluation.

items.title: IdeaTaste: Do LLMs Share the Research Taste of Human Researchers?
items.why: Introduces a benchmark scoring LLMs on research taste/judgment against real published work, relevant to evaluating higher-order scientific reasoning capabilities of models.

items.title: Quantiles, Not Points: Streaming Quantile Matching for Ordinal-Aware LLM-as-a-Judge Calibration
items.why: Proposes a new quantile-based calibration method for LLM-as-a-judge scores against human ratings, a concrete adoptable technique for improving judge reliability.

items.title: From Small to Large: Assessing Medical Reasoning, Benchmark Contamination, and Model Size in Language Models
items.why: Investigates whether medical LLM benchmark performance reflects true reasoning versus contamination and question format artifacts, relevant to benchmark validity and eval methodology.

items.title: Sparse Autoencoder Attribution Graphs Are Decided at the Margin
items.why: Empirical study showing SAE attribution graphs are highly sensitive to near-threshold preactivation margins, questioning reliability of a widely used mech interp tool for causal tracing.

items.title: Geometry of Confabulation and Refusal in Small Language Models
items.why: Introduces ConfabQA, a 784-item benchmark isolating refusal-vs-confabulation behavior and probing whether pre-generation hidden states predict and can be steered to prevent hallucinated answers.

items.title: Are Fake Citations a Form of Reward Hacking? A Pre-Registered Study of Post-Training and Citation Cues
items.why: Pre-registered experiment across 12 open-weight checkpoints and four post-training stages testing whether citation fabrication is a measurable reward-hacking artifact of RLHF-style training.

items.title: CREDO: Evidence-Conditioned Credit Assignment for Temporal Reasoning Agents
items.why: Proposes evidence-conditioned credit assignment to fix GRPO's failure to distinguish useful intermediate steps from outcome-only reward, relevant to reward hacking/RL training design.

items.title: MAC-Bench: Benchmarking Multi-Agent Collaboration via Interconnected Tasks
items.why: New benchmark for evaluating multi-agent LLM systems on interdependent, coordination-heavy tasks rather than isolated task difficulty.

items.title: Test-Time Scaling for Open-Ended Reasoning at Small Model Scale
items.why: Proposes a judge-free semantic cluster voting method for test-time scaling on open-ended (non-math) generation tasks at small model scale, extending eval methodology beyond verifiable domains.

items.title: InteractionBench: Measuring Timing, Task Accuracy, Whisper and Volume, and Grounding in Real-Time Voice Systems
items.why: New benchmark and harness jointly measuring timing, task accuracy, paralinguistic control, and grounding in real-time voice systems using shared recorded audio across systems.

items.title: SelfImprove-Bench: Evaluating Generalization in Self-Improving Agents
items.why: New benchmark targeting generalization of recursively self-improving agent pipelines, addressing a gap in reliable metrics for RSI capability claims.

items.title: Same Outputs, Different Scores: Auditing the Unchecked Graders of Multimodal LLM Benchmarks
items.why: Audits inconsistent, unexamined scoring/grading rules across eight multimodal LLM benchmarks, showing published scores can shift based on grader choice—directly relevant to eval methodology validity.

items.title: D&A: Decoupling Description and Assessment Enables VLMs as Zero-Shot Robotic Reward Models
items.why: Proposes a zero-shot VLM-as-reward-model method that decouples description from assessment to avoid confirmation bias/hallucinated success, relevant to reward model design and hacking in RL settings.

items.title: A Survey on Agentic Security: Applications, Threats and Defenses
items.why: A large taxonomy (274 papers) of agentic security covering red/blue-teaming and offensive/defensive eval frameworks for agentic LLM systems.

items.title: Beyond Single-shot Writing: Deep Research Agents are Unreliable at Multi-turn Report Revision
items.why: Introduces Mr Dre, a new benchmark testing whether Deep Research Agents can reliably revise reports from user feedback across multiple turns, exposing a gap in current single-shot eval paradigms.

items.title: Reinforcement World Model Learning for LLM-based Agents
items.why: Proposes a self-supervised method for learning action-conditioned world models to improve LLM agents' planning and adaptation, relevant to agentic RL training methods.

items.title: Activation-Based Active Learning for In-Context Learning: Challenges and Insights
items.why: Tests whether transformer MLP activations can improve in-context example selection for active learning, a mechanistic-interpretability-adjacent method with potential practical adoption.

items.title: SpeechEQ: Benchmarking Emotional Intelligence Quotient in Socially Aware Voice Conversational Models
items.why: Introduces a new benchmark for evaluating emotional intelligence and paralinguistic reasoning in voice conversational models, relevant to human-AI interaction evaluation.

items.title: PredActBench: Benchmarking Tool-Augmented Dialogue under Controlled Tool Noise
items.why: Introduces PredActBench, a benchmark testing tool-calling agents against predictive tools with controlled noise/error rates, addressing the unrealistic assumption of perfect tool reliability in agent evals.

items.title: SWE-Opt: A Benchmark for Evaluating LLMs on Performance-Oriented Repository-Level Optimization
items.why: SWE-Opt is a new repository-level benchmark evaluating LLMs on real-world performance optimization trade-offs rather than isolated functions, a reusable harness for code-eval researchers.

items.title: GraphNIAH: A Benchmark for Long-Context Reasoning over Real-World Graphs
items.why: Introduces a needle-in-a-haystack long-context benchmark built on real-world graph data rather than synthetic text, addressing known contamination/generalization flaws in prior NIAH benchmarks.

items.title: phone-harness/phone-harness (4062★)
items.why: An open-source agent harness (4k+ stars) that lets LLM agents control a phone UI, useful as a testbed for agentic evaluation and reward-hacking studies in mobile environments.

items.title: SimXAI: A Simple Drop-in Layer Increases Interaction Quality and Understanding in Conversational XAI
items.why: Proposes a drop-in LLM-based layer replacing brittle intent/dialogue-management pipelines in conversational explainable AI systems, directly bearing on human-AI interaction design for explanation interfaces.

items.title: From Training Exposure to Membership Evidence: A Controlled Study of OLMo 2
items.why: A controlled re-training of OLMo 2 with known document insertions to rigorously test membership-inference methods, offering a cleaner ground-truth methodology for benchmark contamination research.

items.title: Beyond Public Access in LLM Pre-Training Data
items.why: Applies the DE-COP membership inference attack to paywalled O'Reilly books to test whether OpenAI models recognize non-public training data, relevant to training-data provenance and contamination eval methods.

items.title: AgentCollab: A Self-Evaluation-Driven Collaboration Paradigm for Efficient LLM Agents
items.why: Proposes a self-evaluation-driven multi-model collaboration paradigm for LLM agents trading off execution efficiency against reasoning robustness, relevant to agent evaluation and cost-performance tradeoffs.

items.title: Beyond Plausible Prediction: Safety Sufficiency in Web World Models
items.why: Human evaluation of 3,000 predictions from ten web world models reveals that plausible-seeming predictions often fail to support correct safety decisions, directly relevant to safety evaluation of agentic world models.

items.title: Benchmarking Forecasting Agents on Yesterday's Tomorrows
items.why: New benchmark for forecasting agents using past events with known outcomes, addressing the staleness problem in live forecasting benchmarks—relevant to agentic eval methodology.

items.title: P-ContextBench: From Personal Fact Recall to Personalized Agent Behavior
items.why: Introduces a benchmark for evaluating whether LLMs safely and appropriately use private personal context in agent behavior, a new human-AI interaction/privacy eval harness.

items.title: Confident Fools or Careful Searchers? A Behavioural Study of When LLMs Search Beyond Their Static Internal Memory
items.why: Behavioral benchmark auditing when deployed LLM agents choose to search vs. rely on parametric memory, directly relevant to agentic tool-use evaluation.

items.title: From the Zoo to the BULLPEN: Sample-Efficient LLM Profiling via Multi-Channel Model Embeddings
items.why: Proposes multi-channel model embeddings to cheaply profile many LLM properties without running full benchmark suites, a potentially adoptable eval efficiency tool.

items.title: Characterizing LLM Agent Behaviors in Module Shadowing Environments
items.why: Introduces an evaluation framework to detect and characterize untrusted code execution in LLM agent trajectories, relevant to agent safety/reward-hacking style evals.

items.title: From Representation to Readout: Mechanistic Analysis of Membership Signals in Language Models
items.why: Mechanistic study decomposing membership inference signals into internal representation vs. readout mechanisms in LLMs, directly relevant to interpretability research on memorization.

items.title: GENSTRAT: Toward a Science of Strategic Reasoning in Large Language Models
items.why: Introduces procedurally-generated zero-sum betting games as a contamination-resistant benchmark for strategic reasoning in LLMs, a reusable eval method.

items.title: Can Agentic Code Review Catch Vulnerabilities Before They Are Merged?
items.why: SecPRBench is a new benchmark testing whether agentic code review can catch real-world vulnerability-introducing commits before merge, relevant to evaluating agentic coding capability and potential reward hacking in review tasks.

items.title: StrictPRMBench: A Replayable Evaluation Benchmark for Auditing Fixed-Score PRM Aggregation
items.why: Introduces a benchmark isolating the score-aggregation rule used in best-of-N selection with process reward models, directly relevant to reward hacking and PRM evaluation methodology.

items.title: Mechanistic Interpretability for End-to-End Self-Driving
items.why: Applies sparse autoencoder-based mechanistic interpretability to an end-to-end self-driving model, a new application of SAE interpretability techniques outside LLMs that could inform methodology transfer.

items.title: MIRAGE: Auditing Anti-Muslim Bias in Frontier LLMs Across Reasoning, Agentic, and Time-Coupled Conditions
items.why: New 1,200-prompt benchmark auditing anti-Muslim bias in frontier LLMs across single-turn, reasoning, and agentic deployment-realistic conditions, extending bias evaluation methodology.

items.title: inspect-ai 0.3.287
items.why: Routine point release of Inspect AI (UK AISI's widely-adopted eval harness) with no specific new capability noted, so likely low-value unless changelog details matter to harness maintainers.

items.title: HN: Memdoor: A team of 5 Qwen3.8-27B models beats Fable 5 on LiveCodeBench Hard
items.why: Claims a 5-model ensemble of smaller Qwen models outperforms a larger 'Fable 5' model on LiveCodeBench Hard, relevant to benchmark gaming/ensemble eval tricks though unverified and worth scrutiny for eval validity.

items.title: UKGovernmentBEIS/inspect_ai 0.3.287
items.why: Inspect AI (UK AISI's eval harness) adds runtime hooks to hold/rewrite react() agent conversations at turn boundaries and a reset() for compaction handlers, which affects how researchers build and control multi-turn agent eval loops.

items.title: microsoft/Mage-VL-Cowork
items.why: New vision-language computer-use agent model (hybrid-agent/CUA) relevant to human-AI interaction and agentic eval benchmarks.

items.title: HN: Claude Duet is the first personal-assistant-type harness that feels useful
items.why: Discussion of Claude Duet, a new personal-assistant agent harness gaining real user traction, relevant to studying human-AI interaction design and agentic UX patterns.

items.title: From Error Prediction to Causal Influence: Auditing SAE Features in Multiple-Choice QA
items.why: Tests whether SAE features linked to Gemma 3 errors are merely correlated or causally drive answer choice via logit margin, a concrete method for auditing interpretability claims about SAEs.

items.title: HN: LLM Voice
items.why: High-engagement HN thread on an LLM voice interface, relevant to human-AI interaction modality research even though it's not a formal benchmark.

items.title: Prompt Lottery in LLM-as-a-Judge: Measuring and Mitigating Sensitivity to Syntactic Rephrasing

items.why: Introduces a method to infer an LLM's pretraining data domain mixture purely from its generated text, useful for post-hoc auditing of undisclosed training data.

items.title: Right Answer, Wrong Tokens: Tail-Aware Credit Calibration for RLVR
items.why: Proposes TACO, a credit-assignment fix for GRPO-style RLVR that addresses erroneous tail-token reinforcement, a concrete reward-hacking-adjacent failure mode in RL training.

items.title: Amplitude-Only FFN Intervention for Tool-Structured LLM Inference: Method, Gated Evaluation Protocol, and Cross-Model Empirical Results
items.why: Introduces Amplitude Gating, a training-free FFN activation intervention with a gated evaluation protocol tested across models, relevant to mechanistic interpretability tooling.

items.title: Reasoning Error from Known Fact: Step-Level Self-Consistency Group Relative Policy Optimization for LLMs
items.why: Proposes a step-level self-consistency variant of GRPO to detect and reduce hallucinated reasoning steps during RL training, relevant to RL training dynamics and reasoning faithfulness.

items.title: RefactorPlatform: An Open-Source Harness for Controlled Evaluation of Repository-Scale Refactoring Agents
items.why: Open-source harness isolating design axes (model backbone, tooling, etc.) for evaluating repository-scale refactoring agents, a new controlled eval tool for coding agents.

items.title: AlignSAE: Concept-Aligned Sparse Autoencoders
items.why: Proposes SAE training method to align learned features with human-defined concepts, directly addressing the feature entanglement problem that limits practical mechanistic interpretability work.

items.title: Similar Models, Broken Odds: Where Luce's Axiom Fails in Chatbot Arena
items.why: Shows Bradley-Terry ranking in Chatbot Arena systematically misjudges near-duplicate models, a concrete flaw in a widely-used LLM leaderboard methodology.

items.title: Fantastic Metrics and How to Find Them: Meta-Evaluating Metrics for Multi-lingual Style-Personalized Generation
items.why: Proposes a regression-based meta-evaluation framework showing correlation-based metric/LLM-judge validation is unreliable, directly useful for designing better eval metrics.

items.title: Tail Competition Explains Scaling in Best-of-N Sampling for Verifiable Problems
items.why: Provides a theoretical account of why Best-of-N inference scaling works via extreme-value competition between correct/incorrect reward tails, relevant to RL/inference-time scaling and reward model limitations.

items.title: Are We Really Measuring Forgetting? Pitfalls in Evaluating Machine Unlearning for Multimodal LLMs
items.why: Identifies methodological pitfalls in how machine unlearning is measured for multimodal LLMs, relevant to rigorous eval design beyond just capability benchmarking.

items.title: Sparse Autoencoders for Mechanistic Interpretability in NLP: A Critical Survey of Recoverability, Interpretability, and Utility
items.why: A critical survey of 138 SAE studies assessing recoverability, interpretability, and utility claims, useful for calibrating confidence in SAE-based mechanistic interpretability methods.

items.title: ListQA: A Benchmark for Evaluating List-Formatted Factual Knowledge Retrieval in Large Language Models
items.why: A new benchmark targeting list-formatted multi-fact retrieval, a factual knowledge eval dimension not covered by existing single-answer QA benchmarks and could be adopted broadly.

items.title: Diagnosing and Correcting Reward Hacking in Verifiable Instruction Following
items.why: Shows frontier models get full credit on verifiable instruction-following benchmarks despite substantively empty answers, demonstrating a concrete reward-hacking failure mode in verifier-based training/eval.

items.title: $\tau$-Emotion-Bench: Exposing the Interaction Fragility of LLM Agents through Real-World User Emotions
items.why: Introduces a tool-calling agent benchmark that injects realistic user emotional variation to test interaction robustness, directly relevant to human-AI interaction and agent eval.

items.title: Divergent Paths: Learning an Outcome-Predictive Representation of LLM Agent Trajectories
items.why: Shows agent rollout success/failure separate linearly in action-observation embedding space (up to 0.95 AUROC), a reusable signal for predicting and diagnosing agent task outcomes relevant to RL/reward-hacking analysis.

items.title: Sparse Autoencoders Are a Shared Coordinate System for Symbolic Matching
items.why: Uses sparse autoencoder features as a shared coordinate system to ground neuro-symbolic matching, a concrete mechanistic interpretability application combining SAEs with symbolic reasoning.

items.title: RM-OPD: On-Policy Distillation for Generative Reward Models
items.why: Introduces on-policy distillation for generative reward models to fix reward sparsity and cross-domain interference in mixed-domain RLHF, directly relevant to reward modeling and reward hacking mitigation.

items.title: Is This Just Fantasy? Language Model Representations Reflect Human Judgments of Event Plausibility
items.why: Probes whether LM internal representations track human plausibility/modality judgments (possible vs impossible vs nonsensical), relevant to interpretability and model evaluation of semantic competence.

items.title: Anticipatory Evaluation of Language Models: Predicting LLM Benchmark Scores from Descriptions
items.why: Introduces EVALCAST, a 2,290-example resource and method for predicting benchmark scores from task descriptions before running experiments, a new eval methodology to reduce evaluation costs.

items.title: BTS-AgentBench: A Deterministic, Replayable Pipeline from Read-Only Telemetry Logs to Agent Benchmarks
items.why: Introduces a deterministic compiler turning raw operational telemetry logs into replayable agent benchmarks with source-verifiable answers, a reusable eval harness construction method for agentic LLM evaluation.

items.title: The Instability of Safety: How Random Seeds and Temperature Expose Inconsistent LLM Refusal Behavior
items.why: Shows LLM safety refusal decisions are highly unstable across random seeds and temperature in four instruction-tuned models, directly challenging the validity of standard single-shot safety eval protocols.

items.title: Dual-Evolving Reinforcement Learning for Automated Reward Design
items.why: Proposes a dual-loop RL framework where a proposer learns to design reward structures from its own trial outcomes, relevant to automated reward design and reward hacking research.

items.title: CausalDS: Benchmarking Causal Reasoning in Data-Science Agents
items.why: A new benchmark testing causal reasoning in LLM-based data-science agents, filling a gap between symbolic causal benchmarks and realistic data analysis tasks, useful for agent capability evaluation.

items.title: Rubric Dropout: A Simple Way to Mitigate Reward Hacking in Rubric-as-Reward RL
items.why: Proposes rubric dropout to reduce reward hacking in rubric-as-reward RL training, directly addressing a core reward-hacking failure mode in LLM post-training.

items.title: Mechanistic Circuit Identification for Controllable Data Generation
items.why: Introduces a mechanistic-interpretability circuit identification method to guide controllable data generation, linking circuit analysis to training-data valuation.

items.title: IsoVRBench: Video Reward Modeling Without Human Feedback
items.why: Builds a controlled-intervention benchmark isolating individual video properties (alignment, fidelity, motion) to diagnose what video reward models actually discriminate, an eval methodology transferable to reward-model auditing.

items.title: Beyond Successful Play: Diagnosing Opponent Modeling in Large Language Models
items.why: New benchmark/diagnostic framework testing whether LLM agents use genuine theory-of-mind vs. learned heuristics in repeated hide-and-seek against belief-modeling opponents.

items.title: Evidence-First Agentic Verification
items.why: Proposes evidence-grounded agentic verification to fix rubric judges that overlook evidence or accept unsupported self-reports, directly relevant to RL reward-hacking in agentic settings.

items.title: DuplexAct: How Interactive Are Frontier Full-Duplex Spoken Language Models?
items.why: New benchmark for evaluating action-level interactivity (turn-taking, barge-in, etc.) in full-duplex spoken LLMs, filling gaps in existing human-AI interaction eval harnesses.

items.title: Memory Echo in Single-Agent Long-Term Memory: Lifecycle Evaluation and Provenance-Guided Mitigation
items.why: Introduces a lifecycle evaluation and provenance-based mitigation for 'memory echo' bias in agent long-term memory systems, relevant to human-AI interaction and agent evaluation methodology.

items.title: Benchmarking and Training Reward Models for Cross-Source Evidence Grounding in Search Agents
items.why: Introduces a benchmark and trained reward models for evidence grounding/source credibility in search agents, directly relevant to reward modeling and reward hacking research.
